pr_body:
This commit implements this enhancement:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/63018

Also adds a 'info' command for ngpios, reversed pin and line
name information.

The forms of the gpio commands are now:

        gpio conf device pin ol0
        gpio set device pin 1
        gpio get device pin
        gpio blink device pin
        gpio info device

Device name, pin, configuration and set level sub commands now
are suggested/completed when tab is used.

Pin names are suggested with numbers and if available from the Devicetree
gpio line names.

GPIO pin control is now limited to pins that are not assigned as reserved.

Fixes #63018

issue_context.title: gpio_shell: improve usability
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The gpio_shell doesn't support tab suggest/complete for most sub commands: gpio device, pin, pin level and configuration options.

In the past when using the GPIO shell for board bring up I've had the experience that I needed to read the gpio_shell source code to remind me how to get things to work.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Tab suggest should list sub command options when using the gpio_shell and tab complete should work for those sub commands.

review_comments: You should check for `input[i] == '\0'` as well.

This check happens in the logic. If the strings are different at any stage, i.e. `input[i]=='\0'` and `line_name[i]` doesn't it will exit otherwise if the characters are equal and `line_name[i]=='\0'` it is a match.

I found the logic of this routine hard to follow.  What I've determined is that this will return a list of pin numbers, followed by a list of line-names (if available). 

It looks like you always attempt to convert the pin specifier as a number first, so I don't see the value in listing the pin numbers separately in the auto-complete list.

If line_names_len is 0, then it makes sense to show auto-complete for the valid pin numbers.

Yes true, I was thinking at the time it would be good to give the user the option pin number or line name but at the same time during testing I stopped using the pin numbers and was using line names exclusively. Happy to use line name exclusively when available and fall back to pin numbers when line name is not available unless anyone else disagrees.

Non-blocking comment - This duplicates the logic from `gpio_pin_configure()`, which uses asserts.
As a follow up CL, you could create a helper function for this validation that is used both by the shell command and `gpio_pin_configure()`.
This path bypasses the reserved mask check.
